question.text: An employee's EPF account has been inactive (no contributions) for 5 years. Which of the following correctly describes the current status and implications?

answer.text: The account becomes inoperative after 3 years of inactivity and the balance is forfeited
The account becomes inactive after 3 years but continues to earn interest until claimed

After 5 years of no contributions, while the member is still before retirement, the account is treated as inactive/dormant and continues to earn interest until retirement; inoperative status and SCWF transfer apply only under the workbook-listed conditions (such as 3 years after retirement, permanent migration, or death, and only after 7 years of being inoperative)
The account remains active and continues to earn interest regardless of contribution gaps

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the workbook, an EPF account with no contributions for 3 years is considered inactive/dormant; while the member is still before retirement it continues to earn interest until retirement. "Inoperative" status is tied specifically to 3 years after retirement, permanent migration, or death, and only after 7 years of being inoperative is the balance transferred to the Senior Citizen Welfare Fund (SCWF). The Trap: "Forfeited" is the key trap word — the balance is never permanently forfeited but, where applicable, transferred to SCWF. Equally, inoperative status is not triggered simply by 5 years of missed contributions while still working. Note: When clients change jobs, ensure timely EPF transfer to the new employer's account to avoid dormancy, and use UAN-based transfers wherever possible.
